summary: A fragment of a science fiction novel in which Ray Marlowe, a grubby systems technician on a ship, is approached on a concourse by a stunning young woman, Emma Whiston, a Garden-class passenger. She notices the maintenance rat drone under his foot and they trade awkward, flirtatious banter. Ray explains that systems vets are so called because they maintain the rats, and he introduces himself with a Marlowe detective joke.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, engineer Ray Marlowe awkwardly flirts with passenger Emma Whiston while standing on a maintenance rat drone on a ship concourse.
key_facts: Ray Marlowe is wearing stained coveralls he has worn since his vent expedition.
A message arrived from Katie saying only, "I'm lactose intolerant."
A man with a rat underfoot could get into serious trouble for casually interacting with Garden-class passengers.
Emma Whiston is a blond woman of about twenty with wide blue eyes, wearing a green silk shift.
Emma asks Ray whether he is hurting the animal he is standing on, which she calls his pet.
Ray describes the rats as curious and invasive, and as "pretty much just fancy assed calculators."
Emma guesses Ray is part of the engineering crew; she calls him 'quite grubby' and then apologizes.
Emma offers her hand knuckles up, and Ray gives it an awkward squeeze instead of kissing it.
Ray's formal title is Hardware Systems Technician, First Class.
Physical engineers call the technicians 'veterinarians' because they maintain the rats (drones), an old joke.
Ray's surname is Marlowe, spelled with an 'e', and he says it is more like the detective than the playwright.
Emma asks if Ray is hard-boiled, and the excerpt ends mid-reply.
